user_consequence: On the player and coach-viewing-teammate Stats route, the usable content column is narrower than the design intends on every mobile viewport — roughly 64 of 390 CSS px (16%) is lost to redundant horizontal padding before any card content starts, and the loss doubles again at the md breakpoint.
mechanism: FairwayPlayerStats.tsx:99 wraps <CoachHelmShell> in a `px-4 py-2 md:px-6` container. CoachHelmShell.tsx independently applies its OWN `px-4 ... md:px-6` to its masthead (line 152) AND a second, separate `px-4 py-6 md:px-6` to its body/children wrapper (line 212). Neither wrapper is aware of the other, so the three padding declarations stack: at <768px, children render at 390 - (16+16)*2 = 326px effective width instead of 390-32=358px (single 16px owner) or 390 (shell handling its own gutter once).
expected: One padding owner for the Stats route's horizontal gutter (either the route wrapper or the shell, never both).
actual: Route wrapper (FairwayPlayerStats) and shell body (CoachHelmShell) both apply independent horizontal padding to the same nested container.
proposed_fix: Make CoachHelmShell padding-agnostic (children fill 100% width) and let the route-level wrapper (or CoachHelmShell itself, exclusively) own the single gutter; or have CoachHelmShell accept `bare`/`noPadding` and have FairwayPlayerStats stop wrapping in its own px-4. This is a C08/design-system decision — A03 should approve the single-owner pattern since CoachHelmShell is mounted by ~15 surfaces.
accessibility_check: NOT_RUN — no runtime to measure computed widths; verified via source only.

user_consequence: A player (or coach viewing a teammate) on /golf/dashboard/stats sees the single 'Overview' sub-nav tab rendered as the CURRENT page (green text, gliding underline, aria-current="page"), even though clicking it navigates AWAY to a completely different route (/golf/dashboard/coachhelm). Screen-reader users are told they are already on 'Overview' while they are actually on Stats.
mechanism: CoachHelmSubNav.tsx's PLAYER_TABS has one tab, href='/golf/dashboard/coachhelm' (line 134). resolveTabFromPath (lines 146-172) for a single-tab strip matches ONLY an exact pathname === href (line 157-160); since the actual pathname is '/golf/dashboard/stats', it returns null, so `resolved` falls back to the SSR `active` prop. FairwayPlayerStats.tsx:101 always passes `active={activeTab}` which for a player is 'brief' (line 86) — the ONLY tab in PLAYER_TABS — so the tab renders active/aria-current='page' (CoachHelmSubNav.tsx:280,289) unconditionally on the Stats route, which is not actually the Overview route.
expected: aria-current='page' and the active-tab visual treatment are reserved for the route the user is actually on; a strip used purely as breadcrumb/context chrome on a foreign route should not claim to be the current page.
actual: The Overview tab always renders as the current page on the Stats route because the SSR `active` fallback is unconditional and the exact-match resolver correctly returns null but is overridden.
proposed_fix: FairwayPlayerStats should not pass an `active` tab that claims a page it isn't on; either introduce a distinct non-tab breadcrumb rendering (CoachHelmShell already supports `breadcrumbs`) for cross-context routes like Stats, or have CoachHelmSubNav accept an explicit `identityOnly`/`contextLabel` mode that shows the CoachHelm affiliation without an aria-current lie.
accessibility_check: aria-current='page' is asserted on an element whose href does not match window.location — a WCAG 4.1.2 name/role/value mismatch. NOT independently re-verified with an axe run (NOT_RUN, no runtime).

user_consequence: A player or coach who switches the round-scope picker (or the player itself, for a coach browsing the roster) more than once before the first request finishes can end up looking at stats for the WRONG scope — the screen silently shows stale data for a round/player they already navigated away from, with no indication anything is wrong.
mechanism: `loadAll` (StatsSpineStage.tsx:122-178) carries no request generation counter, AbortSignal, or 'am I still current' guard. It is invoked from a `useEffect` keyed on [playerId, scopeRoundId] (line 180-182) and again directly from onClick retry handlers (lines 361,420,503,529). If two invocations overlap (e.g. selecting round A then quickly round B before A's `getPlayerStatsDashboardBundle` resolves), JS resolves promises in COMPLETION order, not call order; whichever call's `.then`/`finally` executes last unconditionally calls every setState (setDetailedStats, setStandingRows, etc., lines 129-177) with no check that its own `id`/`roundId` still matches the current `scopeRoundId`/`playerId` state. The slower, older request can overwrite the newer, correct one. The underlying server action (`stats-dashboard.ts`) also accepts no AbortSignal/generation param, so there is no cancellation path at any layer.
expected: Per C02/T03: reject/discard a request whose scope no longer matches the current selection when it resolves out of order.
actual: No generation/cancellation guard exists in `loadAll` or its call sites.
proposed_fix: Add a request-generation ref (increment on every loadAll call; capture at call time; only apply setState if the captured generation === current ref) — the same pattern the round-options effect at lines 186-207 already correctly uses via its `cancelled` closure flag. Reuse that exact idiom in `loadAll` rather than inventing a new mechanism.

user_consequence: Retrying a single failed optional section (the putting/approach leak maps) throws away the entire visible Stats page — spine, bento, every drill — and replaces it with a full-page skeleton for the duration of refetching all 8 reads, even though only one of those 8 reads failed. Switching the round-scope picker does the same full-page blank-out even though most of the bundle (standing, trends, patterns) is cross-round and unaffected by the switch.
mechanism: `onRetryLeak` passed into PuttingDrill and ApproachDrill (StatsSpineStage.tsx:503,529) is `() => void loadAll(playerId, scopeRoundId)` — the SAME full-bundle loader used for the initial mount, not a scoped retry of only `getPlayerLeakMaps`. `loadAll` unconditionally sets `loading=true` at its very first line (123), and the `loading` branch (lines 342-352) replaces the ENTIRE spine+stage region with two `Skeleton` blocks, discarding the currently-visible, still-valid detailedStats/trendData/standingRows/patterns while only the leak maps needed a retry.
expected: Per T05 and the work order: retry the failing optional region in place; a same-scope refresh must not replace usable content with a full skeleton.
actual: Every retry path — including the leak-map-only retry — calls the same all-8-reads `loadAll` and triggers the same full-page skeleton.
proposed_fix: Give leak maps their own small load/error/retry state (mirroring the existing `leakError` boolean pattern already in place at lines 104,125,171) that calls `getPlayerLeakMaps` alone and patches only `leakMaps`/`leakError`, leaving `loading` untouched. Do the same for the round-scope switch: keep detailedStats/spray (the only two reads that actually depend on `roundId`) behind their own scoped-loading flag rather than the page-wide `loading`.
performance_check: Refetches 8 server reads (up to a combined ~15s worst-case timeout budget per settleWithin calls in stats-dashboard.ts:89-96) to retry 1.

user_consequence: If the full stats bundle fails to load, or the player is judged 'cold start' (no analyzed rounds yet), the round-scope picker disappears — a control that IS mounted through the loading and every success branch vanishes exactly when the user might want to use it to try a different scope or confirm what's being requested.
mechanism: The `loadError` branch (StatsSpineStage.tsx:354-370) renders only a `Surface`+`InlineNotice`+Retry button — `roundPicker` (built at lines 310-340 and otherwise rendered in the loading branch at 345, the scoped-round branch at 406, and the success branch at 577) is omitted. The `isColdStart` branch (462-478) likewise omits it. Note this is narrower than the Section 12 seed's exact wording ('some error/empty branches omit it') — the LOADING branch does correctly keep it mounted (line 345); only the hard-error and cold-start branches drop it.
expected: A control that stays mounted through loading/success stays mounted through its own page's error/cold-start states too, per the file's own comment at lines 299-309 explaining why it must not vanish.
actual: loadError and isColdStart branches omit roundPicker.
proposed_fix: Render `roundPicker` above the InlineNotice in the loadError branch too (it is already independent of `detailedStats`/etc.). For isColdStart, render it only when `roundOptions.length > 0` (a coldStart player can still have scorecard-only rounds with no shot detail — roundOptions is populated by a SEPARATE fetch, `getPlayerRoundOptions`, independent of the bundle that determines isColdStart) rather than assuming zero-shot-detail implies zero rounds.

user_consequence: The CoachHelm player-home prediction sentence reads 'Predicted to shoot 74.2 at 78% confidence.' A reasonable reader takes that as '78% chance of shooting exactly/close to 74.2 strokes.' The system does not compute that quantity.
mechanism: `buildPredictionVerdict` (buildPlayerHomeViewModel.ts:144-159) concatenates the point estimate and the confidence percent into one sentence with no distinguishing clause. The confidence value it formats (`data.prediction.calibratedConfidence ?? data.prediction.confidence`, PlayerCoachHelmHome.tsx:290) traces to `performance-predictor.ts`'s `calculateConfidenceInterval` (lines 396-421), which sets a fixed 0.6/0.7/0.8 tier from the player's score stdDev — an 80%-style confidence-INTERVAL width, not a point-probability — and is then optionally recalibrated by `confidence-calibrator.ts`'s bucket lookup, which measures `was_accurate` = `direction==='accurate' || withinInterval` (outcome-validator.ts:19-55,487) against actual outcomes. So the number genuinely means '~78% of past predictions in this confidence tier had the true score within/near the stated range' — a defensible, empirically calibrated interval-hit-rate — but the UI sentence structure implies it is the probability of the single displayed point value.
expected: Per the work order: 'Do not display a percent as likelihood of a score unless that is its supported interpretation.'
actual: Sentence structure attaches the % directly to the point estimate with no interval/range framing.
proposed_fix: Either surface the actual predicted range (predictedRangeLow/High already computed by performance-predictor.ts:212,238 and persisted at line 507-508) alongside the confidence (e.g. 'Predicted 72-77 strokes (78% of similar predictions land in this range)'), or reword to 'this type of prediction has been accurate ~78% of the time' — an interval/track-record framing instead of a point-probability framing. Not a code defect in the calibration engine itself, which is real (Brier score + ECE tracked, DB-persisted, nightly cron) — the gap is purely in the display sentence.

user_consequence: The Stats spine's Fairways/Greens/Putts rows sit next to a single 'Rounds' count, implying all four numbers share that sample size. They don't — each is computed over a different, unstated denominator — so a player cannot tell how many actual data points back the Fairways% versus the Putts/round figure.
mechanism: `buildLedger` (buildStatsViewModel.ts:149-168) emits exactly 4 rows: Rounds (roundsPlayed), Fairways (fairwayPct), Greens (girPct), Putts/rd (puttsPerRound) — with no per-row sample/denominator field in `SpineLedgerRow`. The canonical calculator computes each over a DIFFERENT population: `fairwayPercentage = safePercent(fairwaysHit, fairwayOpportunities)` (golf-stats-calculator-shots.ts:2617) excludes par-3 holes from the denominator; `girPercentage = safePercent(girTotal, girOpportunities)` (line 2636) uses its own opportunity count; puttsPerRound divides by a separate holes-with-recorded-putts denominator (comment at line 1860-1870). None of `fairwayOpportunities`/`girOpportunities`/the putts denominator, nor a timestamp/calc-version, is threaded from `GolfStats` into `LedgerInput`/`SpineLedgerRow`, so the UI cannot express 'Fairways: 61% (n=142 attempts)' distinctly from 'Rounds: 18' the way `PlayerStandingRow.team_n` already does for the team-average comparison (stats-leak-maps-types.ts:64) — that field similarly isn't rendered anywhere in the Spine/Bento/Standing views I read.
expected: Per C07: sample/completeness should be carryable per metric, not implied by an adjacent, differently-scoped count.
actual: One shared 'Rounds' figure is the only sample-size context for four differently-denominated metrics; team_n exists on standing rows but is never rendered.
proposed_fix: Thread `fairwayOpportunities`/`girOpportunities` (already computed, just not exported through LedgerInput) into SpineLedgerRow as an optional secondary caption, and render `team_n` in the Standing drill/track where a team comparison is shown. This is additive (new optional fields), not a rewrite of the calculator.
owner_lane: A06 (adapter), A10 (independent semantics review per boundary)

user_consequence: A player's Stats spine and the CoachHelm team-board can disagree about how fresh the numbers on screen are, with no way for the player to tell.
mechanism: `TeamStatsBoard` (a coach-facing team-wide surface, not directly in my StatsSpineStage/CoachHelmShell mount chain but sharing the same standing/leak-map data family) explicitly threads and renders a freshness string ('stats cache as of ... · rank snapshot as of ...', teamStatsFreshness.ts:33,37) with a stale flag. `PlayerStandingRow`/`PlayerLeakMaps` (stats-leak-maps-types.ts) carry NO computed_at/snapshot timestamp field at all, and none of Spine/Bento/StandingDrill render any freshness/validity-state indicator for the player Stats surface. Whether the underlying standing/leak-map reads are themselves live vs. a periodic snapshot could not be confirmed without the database (BLOCKED, A10).
expected: Per C07, a validity-state/timestamp field should be consistently available wherever a metric might be a snapshot rather than a live read.
actual: One sibling surface (team board) carries freshness; the player Stats surface's equivalent data types do not.
proposed_fix: If `golf_player_standing`/leak-map tables are populated by a periodic job (needs A10 confirmation), add the same `computed_at`/staleness contract PlayerStandingRow/PlayerLeakMaps carry today implicitly through team-board's parallel types.
